components.description: Federal FMLA leave as administered by Clemson: up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a calendar year for the birth of a child and bonding, adoption or foster placement, the employee's own serious health condition, or care of a seriously ill spouse, child or parent. Paid sick, annual, grant personal and compensatory balances must be used concurrently; the remainder is unpaid.

components.description: Under SC State Human Resources regulation 19-712.01, an employee may request leave of up to 180 calendar days for any extended period of certified disability due to illness, injury or maternity; for an employee in an FTE position the agency may not deny the request for bona fide illness or disability. components.description: Modified duties at unchanged compensation for up to 18 weeks (the equivalent of an academic semester) per family event, for a faculty member who has or shares primary caregiving responsibilities for a newborn or a recently adopted or placed child (or is primary caregiver for a seriously ill family member). Released duties are replaced by substitute non-teaching duties (research, course and curriculum development, graduate supervision, service). Requested and approved by chair, dean and Provost; not guaranteed. Must be completed within 12 months of the birth or placement.

faculty_group: All regular full-time equivalent (FTE), temporary time-limited, and temporary grant faculty members are eligible to request an FSAP.
entitlement: Eligible faculty members may request, and supervisors are encouraged to grant, an FSAP in the following circumstances:
A modified workload is not guaranteed and will depend on the circumstances and needs of the department in which the faculty member works and the job duties of the faculty member.
The Provost’s final decision approving or denying the FSAP will be returned to the faculty member and the faculty member’s dean.
duration: A period of modification may be requested and approved for no more than 18 weeks (the equivalent of an academic semester) per family event or situation.

Intermittent modifications may be permitted so long as the total duration in which intermittent modifications are taking place does not exceed the maximum period of 18 weeks per family event or situation.
pay_fraction: A faculty member who has been granted modified work duties under these guidelines will continue to be employed in the same status and at the same level as before the plan was implemented and compensation will remain the same.
Because a modified workload under these guidelines will not impact salary, the faculty member must be given modified duties that are commensurate with existing salary and status.
relief: The plan must describe the specific duties from which the faculty member will be relieved and the specific work to be done in its place

Substitute duties might include: preparation of research proposals, papers, and course materials; devotion of full-time effort to research; development of curricula and/or course materials; work on accreditation and/or certification materials; supervision of graduate student research; and academic service that is compatible with the need for modified work duties.
That is, the faculty member should not be asked to make up released duties before or after the period of modified duties.
time_window: In the case of a request for modification of duties due to birth, adoption, or placement of a child, the FSAP must be completed within the 12-month period following the birth, adoption, or placement of the child.
use_limit: Absent extraordinary circumstances, a request for an FSAP may be granted no more than once per rolling 24-month period for each faculty member.
sequence: An eligible faculty member may request an FSAP instead of or in addition to using FMLA leave.
dual_employee_rule: Two faculty members involved in the same family event or situation, who are employed in the same department, and who have both requested an FSAP for the same period of time, should be accommodated by their department unless management rules it would cause an undue hardship.
medical_certification_note: Departments must consult the Office of Human Resources to discuss whether supporting medical documentation is required to support a request.
notice: faculty members are encouraged to speak with their supervisors as soon as possible about the need for an FSAP.

notes: Chain, birth parent: SC Reg. 19-712.01 extended disability leave (maternity) up to 180 calendar days (c2), with FMLA 12 weeks concurrent from its start (c1) and own sick leave within FMLA (c5) -> (discretionary) renewal/extension (c3), within a 365-day total (leave_limits) ; FSAP modified duties up to 18 weeks (c9) also_available with FMLA, no order stated; course stacking (c16) in lieu of the FSAP release.

Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA 12 weeks (c1), with family sick leave up to ten calendar days per year within it (c5) ; FSAP modified duties up to 18 weeks (c9) also_available with FMLA; course stacking (c16) in lieu of the FSAP release. c2 and c3 are birth-parent only (own disability), so the c1-c2 link is ignored for this role.
No employer-paid parental, maternity or childbirth leave is found in any saved document; pay during leave comes only from the employee's own sick and (12-month faculty) annual balances.

Calendar: the Faculty Manual (IX D2c) states 'A semester is normally 15 class weeks in length, exclusive of final exams'; the FSAP guidelines call 18 weeks 'the equivalent of an academic semester'. No component is stated in semesters, so the calendar does not affect any figure.

Document dates: the FSAP guidelines are dated August 2016 (capture 2017-05-19, before the reference academic year); no later version was saved and the FM 2017-18 does not contradict it; read as in force on 2018-02-22. The FMLA packet (May 2016) and extended leave form (Revised 2016) were current on the reference date per their version notes.

Not components: sabbatical leave (FM IX H; for professional projects, not usable for a birth); court and funeral leave and paid holidays (HR summary; not usable for a birth); the annual-review rule that official leave is excluded from the evaluated year (FM IV E1a-i; not a leave, pay or clock provision); compensatory time (named on the FMLA form, no faculty terms).

The FSAP states 'A faculty member's tenure clock will continue unless the faculty member requests otherwise and the department agrees to stop the clock' and refers to the Faculty Manual for extensions; coded from the Faculty Manual (c10-c12).

Cross-references named but not saved: SC State Human Resources Regulations (reg. 19-712.01); Clemson University Personnel Policies and Procedures Manual / Human Resources Policies and Procedures Manual; Family Support and Accommodation Plan Request Form; Lactation Support Policy; Telecommuting Policy; Temporary Light Duty Return to Work Program; Workweek Policy; long-term disability plan documents; Board of Trustees Manual; Student Handbook, Undergraduate and Graduate Announcements; Athletic Council Policies and Procedures; IBS Policy.
